section_1.title: Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems
section_1.content: Introduce linear systems as the intersection of geometric objects (lines/planes). Explain that a solution exists only where these objects meet. Visualize a 2D system as two lines intersecting at a point.
section_1.example: Imagine two smart-robots (A and B) moving along paths defined by equations. Their collision point is the unique solution to the system.

section_2.title: The Role of Inverse Matrices
section_2.content: Explain that an invertible matrix represents a transformation that doesn't collapse dimensions. If a matrix is invertible, the 'robot's' path can be perfectly reversed. Connect this to the determinant: non-zero determinant = space is preserved.
section_2.example: Think of an invertible matrix as a 'transformation gate' that stretches a square grid. The inverse matrix is the 'undo button' that snaps the grid back to its original shape.

section_3.title: Column Space: The Reachable World
section_3.content: Define Column Space as the span of the column vectors. It is the set of all possible 'destinations' the transformation can reach. Use a 3D animation showing vectors generating a plane or a line.
section_3.example: A 3D printer head has three motors. The column space represents every point in the XYZ coordinate system that the printer head can physically reach.

section_4.title: Null Space: The Hidden Dimensions
section_4.content: Explain Null Space as the set of vectors that are 'squashed' to the origin by the transformation. This is the 'hidden' part of the system that disappears during the process.
section_4.example: If a camera lens flattens a 3D scene into a 2D photo, the 'depth' axis that vanishes into the photo's plane represents the null space of the projection matrix.

section_5.title: Synthesis and Summary
section_5.content: Link the concepts: A system has a solution if the target vector lies within the Column Space. If the Null Space is non-trivial, the solution is not unique (multiple paths lead to the same destination).
section_5.example: Review: Inverting a map (Inverse), finding the reachable zone (Column Space), and identifying obscured details (Null Space) are the three pillars of solving complex linear systems.

section_1.title: Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems
lecture_lines: Linear systems are intersections of geometric objects.
Equations define lines or planes in space.
The solution is where these objects meet.
Robots A and B track these specific paths.
Their collision point is the unique solution.
animations: Draw two intersecting lines on a black plane (#FFFFFF).
Draw lines intersecting at a single point (#FFFFFF).
Highlight the intersection point as the solution (#FFFF00).

section_2.title: The Role of Inverse Matrices
lecture_lines: Invertible matrices preserve the geometric dimensions.
They represent a transformation that is reversible.
Non-zero determinants mean space is preserved.
animations: Display matrix A as a square transformation grid [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg] (#FFFFFF).
Display identity matrix I as an unchanged grid [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg] (#FFFFFF).
Animate the transformation of grid A back to identity I [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg] (#FF00FF).

section_3.title: Column Space: The Reachable World
lecture_lines: Column space is the span of column vectors.
It defines all reachable destinations in space.
Think of a 3D printer's reachable range.
Vectors can generate a line or plane.
Every reachable point lies within this span.
animations: Display column vectors as bold arrows from origin (#FFFFFF). [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/printer.svg]
Animate scalar multiplication creating a line (#00FF00).
Show linear combinations forming a plane (#00FF00).
Fill the reachable span as a semi-transparent surface (#00FF00).
Show a target point lying within the shaded span (#FFFFFF). [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/printer.svg]

section_4.title: Null Space: The Hidden Dimensions
lecture_lines: Null space contains vectors squashed to origin.
This hidden part disappears during transformation.
It represents dimensions lost in projection.
animations: Show a matrix mapping diverse vectors to the origin (#FFFFFF) using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg].

section_5.title: Synthesis and Summary
lecture_lines: Solutions exist if vectors span the target.
Non-trivial null space implies non-unique solutions.
Inverse, column space, and null space are key.
